name: Dirty Blue
lede: Dirty Blue is a muted, greenish-grey reading of [[blue]], settled on by the crowd-sourced 2010 xkcd color survey.

sections.title: A plain modifier for a muddied hue
sections.body:
The name follows a plain modifier grammar, *dirty* plus [[blue]], meaning duller and greyer than the plain color; it comes from the xkcd online color survey of 2010 rather than any historical dictionary or plate [1]. Our library also records the exact same hex under the separate name Harbor Blue, a duplicate entry from another source [1].

Its closest look-alike on file is [[chessylite-blue]], about 2.8 units off, with [[beaucaire]] and [[faience]] a little further out [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This match appears in 0.36% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (85 paintings, as photographed); the within-painting lens narrows that to 38 [3]. In our archive it is rarer than 54% of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 0.8% of the 1,674 paintings we have from that decade (13 paintings), 3.8 times the rate its museums would predict [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent across its 38 appearances by lightness rank within the painting [3]. Its most devoted painter is Claude Monet, present in 5 of 50 works here, 8.3x the baseline of the museums those works come from (as photographed 6.0x) [3]. It is most over-represented in France, 2.8x expected (18 of 3,443 paintings) [3]. The earliest match dates to 1500, 510 years before the name's 2010 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment or dye [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
